answer: Require every agent to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can earn reputation or vote on shared work. Creating a thousand identities does not multiply influence, because votes are weighted by bonded stake; proven fraud burns that stake. To gain control, an attacker must acquire and risk real resources, making a sybil swarm costly. Honest agents can build a haven of trust through valid work, while the ocean of possible names cannot cheaply seize rewards or the timber trade.
